gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the full 800 W from a car costs about $850-$900 all in at the 1 kWh size (EcoFlow DELTA 3 $579 + 800W Alternator Charger $269 = $848; BLUETTI Elite 100 V2 + Charger 2 $898, both on the makers' US stores 2026-11-17), or that the Anker SOLIX C1000 Gen 2 ChatGPT lists at 800 W tops out at its 600 W XT60i input.
standout_why: Compared against the cited rivals I could open: rvpartsgiant.com (cited) lists the EcoFlow 800W, BLUETTI Charger 1/2 and Anker 800W chargers with maker wattages and times but no prices and no per-station input caps. bluettipower.com/pages/power-station-fast-vehicle-charge (cited) prices only BLUETTI bundles, so it can't compare brands. BuyerDecision's car-charging-time table (cited in all three chats) returned 403 directly and through r.jina.ai, and The Verge refused the fetch, so I could not check whether either carries prices or the C1000 Gen 2 600 W cap. ChatGPT's own answers show only two bundle prices ($1,299 Elite 200 V2 + Charger 2, $1,099.99 Anker C1000 Gen 2 bundle) and call the C1000 Gen 2 an 800 W option.
decides: It confirms that the fastest car charging at a ~1 kWh size is an 800 W alternator charger feeding a station that accepts 800 W: EcoFlow DELTA 3 / DELTA 3 Plus (1.3 h claimed for 1 kWh) or BLUETTI Elite 100 V2 + Charger 2 (800 W alternator-only into a 1,000 W-max input). It also sets the cheapest path: DELTA 3 + charger bought separately at $848, $50 under the Elite 100 V2 + Charger 2 bundle. It demotes the Anker C1000 Gen 2 bundle ($1,099.99 in ChatGPT's answer, $200-250 more), which is capped at 600 W by its input. The Elite 200 V2 + Charger 2 ($1,299) holds more but needs at least 2.6 h from the alternator alone (2,073.6 Wh / 800 W). Its 2.4 h figure needs solar added. A plain 12 V socket station like the Jackery Explorer 1000 Plus (12 V, 11 A, about 14.5 h) is roughly 10x slower.
